title: sudo: unable to resolve host

source.title: Fixing 'sudo: unable to resolve host' Error in Linux (Linux Handbook)

brief:
**#ops-alerts · 10:12 · pipeline `shop-deploy` failed at step post-deploy**

Yesterday this VM was renamed `app-prod-01` to follow the new naming standard. Since then every `sudo` prints `sudo: unable to resolve host app-prod-01`, and the on-call is worried about what else the rename broke.

The pipeline's last step runs `/opt/ci/post-deploy.sh` as the `deploy` user. It fails although a sudo rule for deploy was added last week (ticket OPS-2981). The developer's suggestion: "just put deploy in the sudo group".

Keep the new hostname. Make name resolution and the deploy rule work with **least privilege**: deploy may restart nginx and nothing else.

tasks.title: Make the new name resolve
tasks.text:
sudo looks up the machine's own name on every call to match host-specific rules. The lookup follows `/etc/nsswitch.conf`: first `files` (`/etc/hosts`), then DNS, and this internal name exists in no DNS.

Compare `hostname`, `/etc/hostname` and `/etc/hosts`. Make `app-prod-01` resolve to this machine without removing the existing entries. Done when `getent hosts app-prod-01` answers with a local address and `sudo true` prints nothing.
hints: `getent hosts app-prod-01` uses the same resolver path as sudo. Empty output means no file or DNS server knows the name.

Ubuntu maps the machine's own name to the loopback alias 127.0.1.1. Append it: `echo '127.0.1.1 app-prod-01' | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts` (or `sudo nano /etc/hosts`; this lab's /etc/hosts is a bind mount, so `sed -i` cannot replace it).

questions.prompt: Which file should map `app-prod-01` to an address on this box?
Which command queries name resolution through NSS, the way sudo does?

checks.describe: the hostname is still app-prod-01, it resolves to this machine, sudo prints no warning

tasks.title: The sudo rule that never loaded
tasks.text:
Run the pipeline step yourself: `sudo -u deploy /opt/ci/post-deploy.sh`. Then compare what the rule file says with what sudo has really loaded for deploy (`sudo -l -U deploy`). Read the comment at the top of `/etc/sudoers` about `@includedir`.

Make the existing rule take effect, check the syntax with visudo, and keep it at mode 0440. Don't add deploy to an admin group. Done when deploy can run `sudo -n systemctl restart nginx`, but not `id`, a shell or other systemctl actions.
hints: `sudo -l -U deploy` lists no rule at all, so the file is never read. sudo skips drop-in files whose name contains a `.` or ends with `~`.

questions.prompt: Which character in the drop-in's file name made sudo skip it?
Which command checks sudoers syntax (and is the safe way to edit sudoers files)?

checks.describe: deploy may run systemctl restart nginx without a password and nothing else; sudoers is valid

walkthrough:
### What was broken
1. The hostname changed to `app-prod-01`, but `/etc/hosts` only knew the old name. sudo resolves the local host name (for `Host_List` matching), the lookup fell through to DNS, failed, and sudo printed `unable to resolve host`. On real servers this can also add a DNS timeout to every sudo call.
2. The rule for deploy was saved as `/etc/sudoers.d/deploy.conf`. sudo's `@includedir` **silently skips** file names that contain a `.` or end in `~` (so editor and package backups are not loaded). visudo does not warn about this.

### Task 1
```bash
hostname ; cat /etc/hostname ; cat /etc/hosts
grep ^hosts: /etc/nsswitch.conf          # files dns
getent hosts app-prod-01                 # empty = nobody knows the name
echo '127.0.1.1 app-prod-01' | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts
getent hosts app-prod-01 ; sudo true     # quiet now
```
*Why:* `getent` follows NSS exactly like sudo and most programs; `dig` and `nslookup` ask DNS only and would mislead you here. If the old name is still listed elsewhere, replace it. On cloud VMs, cloud-init may rewrite `/etc/hosts` (`manage_etc_hosts`), so make the change in its template too.

### Task 2
```bash
sudo -u deploy /opt/ci/post-deploy.sh    # sudo: a password is required
sudo -l -U deploy                        # no rule listed
ls -l /etc/sudoers.d/
sudo mv /etc/sudoers.d/deploy.conf /etc/sudoers.d/deploy
sudo visudo -c                           # all files parsed OK
sudo -l -U deploy                        # (root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart nginx
sudo -u deploy /opt/ci/post-deploy.sh    # nginx restarted
```
*Why:* a rule naming the exact command line is least privilege. Membership of `sudo` would give the pipeline full root. Always edit with `visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/NAME`: a syntax error in any sudoers file can lock everyone out of sudo.

**Source (adapted):** [Fixing "sudo: unable to resolve host" Error in Linux](https://linuxhandbook.com/sudo-unable-resolve-host/): after a hostname change, adding the new name to `/etc/hosts` removed the warning at once. The dotted drop-in name is the documented `@includedir` rule (see the comment in `/etc/sudoers` and `man sudoers`).
